newsitem.title: INDIA: India eases foreign equity limit to woo investors.
newsitem.headline: India eases foreign equity limit to woo investors.

text.p: India said on Thursday it would allow foreigners to own larger shares of firms in various sectors in the latest of a series of moves aimed at fuelling the multi-billion dollar drive for higher growth.

Finance Minister P. Chidambaram told a banking and investment conference that the limit on foreign equity participation for some non-core industry sectors would be raised to 74 percent from 51 percent.
"We are raising the limit (on foreign direct investment) to 74 percent for non-core, non-strategic industries," Chidambaram said.
In his address, Industry Minister Murasoli Maran said freer entry for foreign investors would be particularly encouraged in the infrastructure and export earning sectors.

The high growth rate is needed to stop the country falling into a domestic debt trap and cope with a population of 930 million --the world's second-biggest -- half of whom will be under 25 years by 2000.
India needs around $30 billion to reach government growth targets of 12 percent in industrial production and eight percent gross domestic product during the next few years.
India attracted only $2 billion in foreign direct investment last year.
Maran said more than two-thirds of the $30 billion would have to be raised at home.
"For each dollar of foreign direct investment it will be necessary to raise more than two dollars domestically," he said.

Chidambaram played down concerns that India could fall into a vicious circle of borrowing more from the market to pay its interest obligations. He said the debt service ratio to GDP was currently 26 percent and needed to be 20 percent.
Interest payments currently eat up half the government's revenues.
"The debt is high but not alarming," he said, adding that high growth and widening the tax base should keep it under control.
"It is my job to raise taxes like a bee sucking money from a flower without stinging people," the minister said.
Chidambaram did not give details of the changes on the equity limits. Neither did he specify the list of non-core sector industries in which foreign shareholding could be increased up to 74 percent.

Earlier this week, the Financial Express newspaper reported that mining services, basic metal and alloy industries, electricity generation and transmission were some of the sectors where foreign equity stakes of up 74 percent would be given automatic government approval.
Under the country's company laws, by leaving 26 percent in Indian hands any special resolution by the board of directors can still be blocked by local shareholders, equity analysts said.
Chidambaram said the limit on foreign equity stakes in core sector industries would remain at 49 percent. No foreign participation is allowed in strategic sectors such as defence.
